newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Philippines stars in busy day.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Philippines stars in busy day.

text.p: Top ranked Philippines National Bank on Monday brought a floating rate certificates of deposit issue that set a new standard for the country's bank credits.
Several other issues also launched into a very busy Asian debt market.
Philippine National Bank's US$125 million FRCD issue due in March 2000 was launched at par to float at 65 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return to the top tier is 70 basis points. Lenders have the option to redeem the issue early if the Philippines government holds less than 30 percent of the bank.
HSBC Markets is arranger and bookrunner. Credit Lyonnais, Fuji International Finance (HK) and J.P. Morgan Securities have joined as co-arrangers.
The deal pays 11 basis points less than the bank's prior issue, a three-year FRCD launched last August.
Bankers said that while all Philippine issuers are reaping the rewards of the country's increasingly positive outlook, the top rated banks are benefiting more.
Last week, Coconut Planters Bank launched through BA Asia a US$50 million three-year FRCD that pays 85 basis points, 15 basis points less than its previous issue launched in July 1996.
Coconut Bank also set a US$50 million five-year FRCD that pays 94 basis points all-in.
Unrated China Banking Corp launched a US$60 million three-year FRCD today that pays a coupon of LIBOR plus 85 basis points and an all-in return of 91 basis points.
Bankers are awaiting a five-year floating rate note issue for wholly government-owned Land Bank of the Philippines.
"On a relative basis, we expect Land Bank's deal to be a little tighter than PNB's," remarked a syndicate manager.
In late developments, Thailand announced that it had chosen Salomon Brothers and Lehman Brothers to lead manage its upcoming US$500 million Yankee bond.
In news from Hong Kong, Ka Wah Bank was out with a US$50 million FRCD through arrangers Bayerische Landesbank Hong Kong, HSBC Markets, Bank Austria and NordLB Singapore.
The certificates, which mature in five years but can be put or called after three, pay a coupon of 40 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in return of 58 basis points.
Last June's version paid 63.3 basis points all-in.
Some details also emerged on QPL International's US$100 million FRN.

Also in Hong Kong, Kerry Holding's loan issue was raised to US$750 million from US$500 million in the underwriting stage. Cosco Pacific unit Florens Container mandated BZW to arrange a US$200 million loan.
China's state-owned China Merchants Holdings mandated a US$100 million financing.
Elsewhere, Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers said they will launch a US$1.0 billion global bond for Ford Motor Credit later this week. Goldman Sachs is the bookrunner.
